newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch government bonds digested news of new guilder corporate bond issues to finish higher in trading subdued by holidays in major centres.
Most gains were registered on the opening but the yield discount to Bunds narrowed as guilder state loans lagged their German equivalents.
Dealers attributed the firmer state to a perception Dutch bonds were oversold on Friday, when higher-than-expected October inflation data unnerved investors and traders.
One dealer said the rising inflation differential with Germany justified the closing of the yield spread.
He said the spread could go to eight basis points from 10 now before attracting buyers.
Dealers said the market was unmoved by news of Eurobond issues by retailer Ahold, for 500 million guilders, and insurer Achmea Hypothekenbank, for 250 million guilders.
One trader said the Dutch government's intended absence from the capital markets for the rest of 1996, which has contributed to a fall in yields, could prompt further issuance in guilders.
A broker said rumours last week of a large seller of Dutch paper and the high inflation number continued to unnerve the guilder market today.
She said the closure today of the U.S. market, for Veterans Day, and the French and Belgium markets, for Armistice Day, contributed to the lack of activity.
"I wouldn't expect this market to get going until tomorrow," said the broker.
Dealers said interest was focussed on U.S. October economic data this week with producer prices on Wednesday and consumer prices on Thursday.
